Juxtapose

JUK-stuh-pohz · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To juxtapose place together for contrasting effect.

The photographer chose to juxtapose a picture of the crumbling old mill with one of the gleaming new factory across the river.

Worked Example

The museum wing was designed to juxtapose ancient pottery shards with brand-new 3-D-printed replicas, letting visitors compare the two side by side.

Placing the ancient and modern objects right next to each other, rather than in separate rooms, is exactly what makes this juxtaposition work.

How Juxtapose Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

contrast

contrast: to show a difference between two things

pair

pair: to put two things together, often for comparison

Antonyms

separate

separate: to keep things apart

How Strong Is It? — place near → juxtapose → collide

place near vs. juxtapose

place near vs. juxtapose: To simply place two things near each other says nothing about intent; to juxtapose them is to place them deliberately to highlight a contrast.

collide vs. juxtapose

collide vs. juxtapose: To make two things collide goes further still, suggesting a jarring, almost violent clash rather than a thoughtful contrast.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of juxtapose.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — juxta-

prefix — juxta-: near/beside (Latin)

root — pose

root — pose: to place (French (poser, from Latin ponere))

Put it together

Put it together: Juxta- ('near/beside') plus pose ('to place,' from French poser) gives 'to place beside' -- juxtapose means putting two things right next to each other, usually to highlight contrast.

Use the root in a new word: transpose

Use the root in a new word: transpose: Transpose shares the same 'place' root -- trans- ('across') plus poser, literally to place something across or in a different order.

Root Check

Word Choice

Juxtapose is common in art, writing, and photography criticism -- use it when two things are physically or structurally placed together, not just generally compared.
